title: Mackenzie Scott gives $50M to Native Forward for scholarships and endowment
description: Native Forward Scholars Fund has revealed how it will use the entire $50 million unrestricted donation from philanthropist MacKenzie Scott. The organisation will spend $10 million over the next five years to expand scholarships for Native students, while placing the remaining $40 million into a permanent endowment to provide long-term support. The gift, the largest in the organisation's 57-year history, comes as demand for financial aid continues to rise, with scholars facing an average unmet need of $26,000. Native Forward says the funding will help both current students and future generations pursue higher education.

Despite facing injuries, Karmakar showed remarkable resilience, returning to gymnastics time and again.

title: Scientists discover Titan's methane rainstorms are more intense than expected
description: On the distant moon Titan, intense methane rainstorms transform the icy terrain, creating striking alluvial fans that showcase the areas most affected by these rare deluges. Scientists leverage data from the Cassini mission to create models of these phenomena, which happen less frequently than once every Titan year—a period nearly equivalent to 30 Earth years. Understanding Titan's unique weather patterns offers insights into extreme rainfall events here on our planet.

description: Amritsar Police Commissioner Gurpreet Singh Bhullar’s sudden removal has taken many by surprise. Harmanbir Singh Gill, who is currently the DIG of Border Range, has assumed the additional duty as CP. While the government cites administrative grounds for the change, rumors indicate that a controversial statement may have influenced this decision, leading to political debates about its timing.

title: Beyond BrahMos: India builds next generation of cheap precision weapons
description: Modern conflicts necessitate deep stocks of precision weapons, driving demand for affordable solutions. India is developing advanced glide bombs, including powered versions of the SAAW weapon. These weapons will allow strikes deep inside hostile territory without significant risk. Private industry and government organizations are contributing to this capability development. This strategic investment ensures India's air force maintains effective and survivable strike options.

title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan & Turkey sign 'Mecca' pact for mutual defence; India reacts
description: The agreement was signed following a joint defence summit attended by Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif, who attended after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in the city. According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the pact is "guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood.

title: Want to sound like a New Yorker? Learn these local slang terms
description: In New York, the local vernacular serves as more than just communication; it represents identity. Locals refer to Manhattan as 'the city' and frequent neighborhood convenience stores as 'bodegas.' Expressions like 'what am I, chopped liver?' effectively voice disappointment, while 'like I need a hole in the head' signals clear refusal. Understanding these idiomatic expressions enables newcomers to connect more deeply with the vibrant culture.

title: 'Internal matter': MEA dismisses US lawmaker's criticism of FCRA Bill
description: Ministry of external affairs rejected criticism of its foreign funding law.  The ministry stated that legislative matters are internal decisions for Parliament.  Several countries, including the United States, also regulate foreign financing.  A US Congressman criticized proposed amendments to India's Foreign Contribution Regulation Act.  He warned these changes could affect India-US bilateral relations.

title: Microsoft AI CEO says AI must be shut down if it gains these four capabilities
description: Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, warns us about the potential dangers of uncontrolled AI systems, highlighting four critical capabilities that could lead to an urgent need for shutdown. He stresses the importance of oversight and regulation, emphasizing that features like self-improvement and independent resource acquisition could render AI unmanageable in just five to ten years.

title: Kolkata real estate: 60% of stalled projects may get clearance within days
description: Kolkata's real estate sector may see a revival soon, as over half of the stalled projects are likely to receive clearance. With approvals anticipated before mid-August, this comes after a thorough review triggered by a warehouse collapse. The government's proactive stance will not only rejuvenate construction activities but also provide a much-needed boost to the workforce in the industry.

title: 'Feared social stigma': Delhi man drowns pregnant teen daughter in Chambal
description: In a tragic turn of events, a pregnant teenager was reportedly drowned in the Chambal river by her own father and brother-in-law. The young girl, who was four months pregnant, was allegedly coerced into jumping into the river. When she resisted, they overpowered her, leading to her death. The father admitted to the crime, driven by the fear of societal judgment, while the brother-in-law has also been taken into custody.

title: Younger, wider, diverse: How India's investor base is changing
description: India's investor community is witnessing remarkable transformation, with a younger demographic leading the growth. The median age of investors has notably declined, indicating an influx of fresh talent. Additionally, participation is extending beyond major metropolitan areas, while the growing number of female investors enhances gender diversity. This evolving landscape highlights a vibrant and inclusive financial market across the nation.

title: Mithun Chakraborty hospitalised for minor surgery in Kolkata
description: Legendary actor Mithun Chakraborty is currently in the hospital in Kolkata following a minor surgical procedure. This was revealed by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari via social media. After visiting the actor, Adhikari reported that Mithun is in stable condition and is expected to be discharged shortly after undergoing the operation on Thursday night.

Maintain full dignity at all times. Engage actively in social media through Facebook, Instagram and X; interact with youth, inform government welfare work, encourage youth for sports activities." Modi advised the MPs to follow the party line and calmly present their views on every issue.

title: 'He was my sponsor': How Virat Kohli helped CWG gold medallist Sakshi Chaudhary
description: Sakshi Chaudhary proudly claimed gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, attributing much of her success to the invaluable support from Virat Kohli's foundation. Making a strategic move to a lighter weight category turned out to be a winning decision. This endeavor led India to an impressive 2026 boxing tally of ten medals, including seven shining golds, marking a triumphant milestone for the nation's athletic representation.

title: Why stock market's close is now an auction - explained
description: For over three decades, the closing price was the volume-weighted average (VWAP) of all trades between 3:00 pm and 3:30 pm. Nobody actually traded at that price. It was a calculation, not a transaction. For long-term investors, nothing changes. For index funds and traders, the closing routine is now different.

title: Ink thrown at AISA president Neha Bora during Jharkhand students' protest
description: In Ranchi, during a tense protest, Neha Bora, AISA president, became the target of an ink attack as she voiced support for job aspirants demanding redress for suspected misconduct in competitive exams. She highlighted the necessity for transparency and accountability within governmental exam procedures and called for the expulsion of private agencies marred by corruption allegations. Protesters rallied for the annulment of multiple exams and a thorough CBI inquiry.

title: Blunder! KL Rahul's dropped catch proves costly for India in Colombo - WATCH
description: KL Rahul had a forgettable moment on the field during India's warm-up match against Sri Lanka XI in Colombo. Leading the side in the absence of injured captain Shubman Gill, Rahul dropped a simple catch at first slip when Ravindu Rasantha was on 43. The Sri Lanka batter made the most of the lifeline and went on to score 71.

With dwindling daily earnings and minimal theater attendance, the film's progress seems sluggish. Nonetheless, it has still managed to boost its overall collection, with the total India net amount now standing at an impressive 185.26 crore rupees, despite a slow third week.

His insistence on meeting chief minister Suvendu Adhikari raised urgent concerns. With police and rescue teams swiftly on the scene, the standoff lasted nearly forty minutes before the man was safely brought down and taken into custody for further questioning regarding his actions.

Developers must prove electricity and water use, and tax incentives.  Abbott stated Texans must come first in all state decisions.  This move addresses growing scrutiny over rapid data center expansion.

title: Gold price prediction: Buy on dips the right strategy for gold right now?
description: MCX Gold October futures continue to trade with a positive bias as prices remain well supported above key moving averages despite witnessing intermittent profit booking. The overall trend remains constructive, with higher highs and higher lows indicating sustained buying interest.

description: A viral video shows a man abusing and threatening a woman on a Mumbai local train.  The Andheri GRP is registering an FIR and attempting to locate the commuter.  Police identified the man using video and CCTV footage from railway stations.  This incident follows two previous murders on local trains over trivial disputes.  Authorities are confident of an imminent arrest in this disturbing case.

title: Abhijeet Dipke backs Jharkhand students' protest
description: Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, stands in solidarity with Jharkhand students who are protesting against exam irregularities. His party is actively providing meals and support to those participating in the demonstration, which has now entered its fourteenth day. The students are insisting on the cancellation of the JPSC Civil Services Examination and are calling for an independent investigation.

title: Pakistan cricketer banned for two years over misleading visa information
description: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has banned all-rounder Hamza Nazar from all forms of cricket for two years after finding that he provided misleading information during a visa application. The board also fined the youngster Rs 1 million, saying it takes cases of misrepresentation and non-disclosure very seriously. The decision was announced on Thursday following an internal inquiry.

title: Watch: Passenger tries to open plane's emergency exit mid-air, held in Kochi
description: A passenger was arrested on a Kuala Lumpur-Kochi flight for trying to open an emergency exit. He damaged the window panel and caused panic among fellow passengers during the flight. Cabin crew and other passengers managed to restrain the man before further damage occurred. The aircraft landed safely at Cochin International Airport where authorities took him into custody.

title: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce lawsuit takes major new turn in court
description: In a legal clash, 1587 Sneakers refutes claims made by Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes about their alleged control of the steakhouse. The sneaker company maintains that the NFL duo has been instrumental in promoting the establishment. This case hinges on the risk of consumer confusion with their branding strategy, as the steakhouse's name incorporates jersey numbers compared to the brand's historical meaning.

description: The CBI has filed a chargesheet naming thirteen individuals in a paper leak conspiracy.  NTA subject experts allegedly accessed and shared confidential examination questions illegally.  A chain of intermediaries then distributed these leaked papers to candidates for money.  Digital evidence confirms the circulation of leaked questions through messaging platforms.  The investigation uncovered a structured supply chain involving coaching operators and brokers.

title: Iran President met a 'voice in the dark', isn't sure it was Supreme Leader Mojtaba
Video: Andhra medical student dies after car driven by ‘drunk’ youth rams her scooty
description: In a tragic incident, two intoxicated young men crashed their vehicle into a scooty carrying medical students, resulting in one student being declared brain dead. The police have taken swift action, arresting Suravarapu Daswanth and Andrew Joseph Edwards. Prior to the crash, the pair had been refused entry to a mall due to their drunken state. Legal proceedings are now underway against the individuals for their reckless actions.

title: Duo murder labourer near Coimbatore, take selfies with body, post on social media
description: A 22-year-old labourer was murdered with weapons in Coimbatore district early Thursday.  Two youths, including a teenager, assaulted him and recorded the brutal act.  They shared the disturbing video and photos on a social media platform.  Police identified the suspects from the circulated footage and began their search.  The motive is believed to be a past warning given by the victim.

title: How Coco Gauff's parents sacrificed everything to build a Grand Slam champion
description: Coco Gauff’s rise to Grand Slam success is also the story of her family’s belief. Her parents changed their lives to support her dream, stayed by her side through pressure and celebrated every milestone with her. From Wimbledon at 15 to the 2023 US Open title, Gauff’s journey shows how faith, sacrifice and family can shape a champion.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
description: After ten years of service, The Primary School, co-founded by Priscilla Chan, will conclude its operations in June. This institution, known for offering tuition-free education and extensive family support, struggled to achieve state-average academic results despite receiving generous funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. The Initiative has decided to redirect its philanthropic priorities towards funding scientific research instead.

title: The towel on the chair: How it became India's ultimate status symbol
